    <h1>The short life of orthopositronium</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
Positronium is a bound state of an electron and a positron, similar to a hydrogen-like atom. Its states are classified by the total spin:

- *parapositronium* (spin 0) decays mainly into two photons;

- *orthopositronium* (spin 1) decays into three.

In this project you will study the decay mechanism of orthopositronium, estimate its lifetime and see how QED describes the decay of composite particles.

- Consider the decay of orthopositronium into three photons, $o\text{-Ps} \to 3\gamma$, assuming that the electron--positron system is at rest (the approximation $v \ll c$).

(a) Draw all six tree-level diagrams of the process. Explain why there are exactly six. Write the full matrix element $\mathcal{M}$, taking into account that the photons are identical.

(b) Compute the squared matrix element $|\mathcal{M}|^2$, averaged over the initial and summed over the final spins, in the approximation of fermions at rest ($\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{p}'=0$).

(c) Find the differential decay rate in the energy of one of the photons, $$\frac{d\Gamma}{d\omega_1},$$ where $\omega_1$ is the energy of the first photon in the center-of-mass frame. Take the symmetry of the process into account.

(d) Integrate and obtain the total decay width $\Gamma(o\text{-Ps} \to 3\gamma)$. Using $$\tau = \frac{\hbar}{\Gamma},$$ find the lifetime of orthopositronium in vacuum.

(e) Modify the calculation assuming that the electron and the positron are in the ground state of a hydrogen-like atom (wave function $\psi(0) \neq 0$). How does this change the result?

:::
